examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: To disprove regularity, assume a pumping length p and choose a word depending on p. Every legal split xyz with |xy|≤p and |y|>0 must fail for some pumping count. The adversary chooses the split; exhibiting only one bad split is insufficient. Intersecting with a regular language can isolate a simpler nonregular subset.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
For aᵖbᵖ with p=5 and a legal pumped part y containing 2 a's, how many a's occur when y is pumped three times?

**Answer: 9.** The original has 5 a's and one copy of y. Three copies add two extra copies, each of length 2, yielding 5+4=9 a's while b-count stays 5. The unequal counts show why that pumped word leaves {aⁿbⁿ}.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
The pumping lemma is necessary, not sufficient, for regularity. Showing a language can pump for selected strings is not a regularity proof.

Showing one convenient decomposition fails is insufficient; handle all permitted decompositions.
